subject: docs/coop/artifacts/distribution-core-inventory-contract.v2.json

shouldFix.title: The required inventory graph cannot assign the allowed shared executable to layers deterministically.
evidence: inventorySchema.everyReleaseMustPublish requires a complete file/dependency/TCB inventory and layer assignment, and dependencyGraph requires digest-pinned nodes with layer assignment.

threeCores.oneExecutableSharing permits the distribution core and semantic host to be one executable; L-DIST is defined over distribution-core bytes while L-HOST is defined over semantic-host authority surfaces and may share the L-DIST process.

The contract defines neither graph-node granularity nor whether layer assignment is exclusive or set-valued, and it gives no representation rule for a single digest-pinned executable spanning L-DIST and L-HOST. It also does not define dependency-edge meaning/direction or graph roots. Repository search found no other definition of these L-* layers or graph rules.
shouldFix.impact: Two successors can produce materially different supposedly complete graphs for identical bytes—L-DIST-only, L-HOST-only, duplicated, or multi-assigned—without violating the text. That prevents reproducible review of the central inventory/layering obligation and risks either collapsing semantic-host authority into the distribution layer or double-counting the closure.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Define node granularity, graph roots, edge relation and direction, layer-assignment cardinality/overlap, and the canonical representation of one executable containing both distribution-core and semantic-host responsibilities while preserving the non-migration boundary. If those rules remain deferred, name their owner/open decision and narrow the claim that this artifact supplies the inventory/layering design contract.

attacks.attack: OD-101-2 launders ownership of core signing/notarization into DR-112 or DR-110.
attacks.evidence: OD-101-2 is RESERVED and owned by a later DR-101 successor. DR-112 recovery ceremony and DR-110 repair-media trust are explicitly adjacent inputs, not owners of core code-signing or OS notarization.

attacks.attack: Source qualifiers are strengthened or dropped.
attacks.evidence: managementOnly retains 'current'; signedDistributionCore retains 'Proposed'; defaultInstall.containsStanding expressly marks the inclusion list PROPOSED; pureEvaluationCore retains 'function'. The carried 30-line source span is exact.

attacks.attack: The decision-column decomposition silently omits inventory or layering.
attacks.evidence: OBL-D-INV maps the verbatim mandatory closure/TCB inventory fragment to everyReleaseMustPublish, and OBL-D-LAY maps the verbatim layering fragment to layerTaxonomy. Language, signing/notarization, and platforms are separately mapped rather than collapsed.

attacks.attack: The candidate treats a T2-02 contract as the entire D-056 path to SATISFIED.
attacks.evidence: The current D-056 text requires five gates. The subject correctly records that gates 2 and 3 still fail: OD-101-1 and OD-101-2 are design work, not execution/measurement, and are not named condition-4/DR-G remainders. It expressly denies that this contract can unlock SATISFIED.

attacks.evidence: The 12d192f7 digest is labeled INHERITED-V1-AUTHORING-PIN with its historical commit, while reMeasurementAtV2 separately records and matches the live b9819d6e digest and current HEAD.

attacks.attack: v2 contains an unrostered semantic change from v1.
attacks.evidence: Recursive v1-to-v2 comparison found no changed leaf outside the explicitly closed repair/succession roster. basedOn, appliesFindingsOf, and honestyRepairsFromV1 make the successor path inspectable.

attacks.attack: The candidate claims SATISFIED, QUALIFIED, application, sealing, or implementation authority.
attacks.evidence: It is non-applied, binds nothing, recommends no seal, keeps DR-101 OPEN, disclaims a qualified small core, and denies authorization of docs/v2/implementation/. This review grants no application-grade acceptance and changes no DR-101 disposition.

attacks.attack: The three meanings of core are collapsed or semantic authority migrates.
attacks.evidence: L-DIST, L-HOST, and L-EVAL remain distinct; process sharing is allowed only with explicit non-migration and non-delegable-authority boundaries. Optional components remain L-COMP.

attacks.attack: The artifact chooses a core language or signing/notarization ceremony.
attacks.evidence: OD-101-1 rejects treating native/Rust framing as a language choice. OD-101-2 imports only proposed signing-role identities; ceremony, thresholds, and OS notarization stay reserved.

attacks.attack: DR-106/DR-109 storage is smuggled into the default install.
attacks.evidence: The subject distinguishes the proposed default management/recovery install from a different authoritative offline signed selection. It explicitly excludes evidence databases and storage backends from the default and preserves DR-106/DR-109 as wholly deferred owners.

attacks.attack: The inventory/graph text pretends a populated per-platform closure already exists.
attacks.evidence: The subject honestly denies that a populated per-OS table exists, so it does not invent execution evidence. But its purported schema still lacks deterministic node, edge, root, and overlapping-layer rules for the expressly allowed shared executable; see DCIC-V2-S1.

attacks.attack: The DR-101 live row or G01-G05 standing is misstated.
attacks.evidence: The DR-101 row is exact. Live file 08 names G01/G02/G05 through D-086 and G03/G04 through D-102, with every harness not authored and not QUALIFIED, matching gatesG01G05.

conclusion: REJECT under the prompt's zero-SHOULD-FIX rule. The claimed v1 repairs withstand attack, but DCIC-V2-S1 leaves the central inventory/layer graph non-deterministic for the expressly allowed shared executable. This is a non-application review only: DR-101 remains OPEN, nothing is SATISFIED or QUALIFIED, and implementation is not authorized.
